sanskrit_verse:
ūnadvivarṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ /
āśmaśānād anuvrajya itaro jñātibhir vṛtaḥ // YajñS_3.1
transliteration: ūnadvi-varṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ / āśmaśānāt anuvrajya itaraḥ jñātibhir vṛtaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: One who has not completed two years shall not perform burial; water libations are to be offered thereafter. Another male relative follows from the cremation ground, accompanied by known kin.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in age-appropriate capacity for ritual execution
Causation aligns with sequential stages of life and death rites
Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for sacramental acts
Restoration logic requires proper succession of familial dharmic roles
Consciousness alignment occurs through correct performance of ancestral duties
executable_legal_axioms: IF age < 2 years THEN ritual_burial_permitted = FALSE
IF cremation_complete = TRUE THEN water_liberation_required = TRUE
IF primary_dharmic_heir_unavailable = TRUE THEN next_kin_must_perform = TRUE
IF known_relations_present = TRUE THEN ceremonial_following_permitted = TRUE
IF all_succession_rules_met = TRUE THEN consciousness_realignment_possible = TRUE
supreme_court_application: In matters concerning inheritance or post-death rituals, the court must recognize that only those meeting specified experiential thresholds may execute sacred rites. Legal standing derives not from mere relation but from qualified participation in Vedic succession.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes chronological fitness as determinant of rite eligibility. Anupūrvaśaḥ reflects natural progression of soul-releasing ceremonies. Responsibility is proportionally assigned based on experiential ripeness, ensuring alignment rather than correction.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Delayed ritual until qualifying period fulfilled
Responsibility assumption protocol: Transfer of duty to eligible heir
Capacity restoration: Observance of preparatory rites before full engagement
Integrity reintegration: Ceremonial affirmation after procedural adherence
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: This law proceeds from Sanatana Dharma's eternal order. No punishment arises where capacity is incomplete—only adjustment toward rightful alignment. Thus is Dharma restored. Consciousness alone is the final arbiter.
